narrative:
Agents have matched 93.8% of October's value automatically, against roughly 62% done by hand in September. NOK 84.7M is still unmatched. Supplier invoices and rebates hold NOK 29.9M of it, store-owner intercompany NOK 14.1M and Intersport inventory and COGS NOK 11.5M.

Most breaks come from the system change, not from errors. The new POS identifies items by EAN while Business Central uses supplier article numbers. Card and Vipps MobilePay settlements arrive net of fees two days after the sale. Rebate credit notes are booked against the season PO instead of the goods receipt.

Each proposed matching rule is learnt from how the controllers cleared the same break by hand in September. Every match is logged with its rule, so the audit trail stays complete without consultant scripts.

signals.title: New POS roll-out — cut-over plan
signals.excerpt: POS replacement rolling out chain by chain alongside the Business Central implementation with Tietoevry. Item master moves to EAN; settlement files change format at cut-over.

signals.title: Reliance on external consultants
signals.excerpt: Close workarounds depend on consultant scripts with limited documentation. Knowledge leaves when consultants roll off.

signals.title: Winter season build — inbound plan
signals.excerpt: Alpine, cross-country and outerwear inbound peaks in October ahead of November and December trading. GRNI and rebate accruals are largest in this window.
